verdict: Hedge 75% of the receivable, which is EUR 6.0M (K1), with an outright EUR/USD forward contract for value 15 June 2027. This follows Treasury Policy v3 s.4.1 (E1). v3 is board-approved (2025-04-22) and states that it supersedes v1 and v2. The 50% figure in the request comes from the superseded v1 (E4, E5). The user's statement could also point to a governance gap, for example v3 never adopted, later rescinded, or changed by the unsupplied v2. That has to be checked before execution (E20). The receivable appears to meet the s.4.1 conditions: it is confirmed, it is about USD 9M equivalent, well above the USD 1M threshold (K6), and it matures in about 216 days, within 12 months (K10, E19). Policy v3 s.4.2 forbids changing the hedge ratio because of management's views on exchange rates (E2). So the treasurer's plan to stay unhedged if she expects the euro to strengthen is not allowed. Any departure from 75% or from forwards needs Audit Committee approval under s.4.3 (E3), and no such approval was found (E20). The requested June 2027 EUR/USD point forecast cannot be reliably determined. Random-walk and professional-forecaster research shows that point forecasts at this horizon have no dependable accuracy (E13, E14). The forecast question can only be framed as the forward plus a range of outcomes. The forward premium has the sign covered interest parity predicts. It is a price shaped by interest-rate differentials, not a market forecast that the euro will rise (E11, E12). The 2026-09-25 bank quote (spot 1.1650, forward 1.1810) is stale and indicative only (E6). Spot has since fallen to about 1.12, and the latest reported close was lower still at 1.1142 on 6 Nov (E8). USD proceeds must therefore be locked in from a live dealable quote. As an illustration only, an interest-parity forward from 1.12 spot is about 1.1291, giving about USD 6.77M on EUR 6M, against USD 7.086M implied by the stale quote (K3, K9, K11, K19). Using the 1.1142 print would lower the illustrative figure further. No implied volatility was found (E17). Under a clearly labelled assumed 8% annualised volatility, a 1-sigma range for June 2027 spot around 1.12 is about 1.051 to 1.189 (K16-K18). Across that range, total USD proceeds are about USD 8.88M to 9.15M with the 75% hedge, against about USD 8.41M to 9.51M unhedged (K20-K24, K6). Confidence is moderate, not high, for three reasons: v3's status and authenticity have not been confirmed against governance records (E20), no live forward or implied volatility was available (E17), and the receivable's timing, credit lines and hedge-accounting election are unknown (E21).

criteriaAssessments.assessment: v3 governs. s.4.1 requires hedging 75% of each confirmed foreign-currency receivable above USD 1M equivalent with maturity of 12 months or less, using forwards (E1). That means EUR 6M (K1), not the EUR 4M (K2) a 50% ratio would give. s.4.2 bars view-based changes to the ratio (E2). s.4.3 requires Audit Committee approval for any deviation (E3). The v1 50% rule (E4) is superseded under v3's own header (E1). The user's 50% premise (E5) matches v1, not v3. Because the user is an insider, the premise could also signal a governance gap (v3 not adopted or rescinded, or v2 changing the rules). This cannot be ruled out from the packet (E20).
criteriaAssessments.mechanisms: Treasury policies use a fixed hedge ratio and ban view-based changes so that treasury cannot take speculative currency positions without board-level oversight. The supersession clause makes the most recent board-approved version govern. The Audit Committee approval step routes any exception to the oversight body instead of leaving it to treasurer discretion.
strengths: v3 text is VERIFIED from the supplied file and states explicitly that it supersedes v1 and v2 (E1)
The ratio, instrument and governance rules are all explicit (E1, E2, E3)
The receivable appears to meet every s.4.1 condition (E19, K6, K10)
weaknesses: v3's authenticity and board approval have not been confirmed against minutes or governance records (E20)
v2 was not supplied, and no later version, rescission or exception could be ruled out (E4, E20)
The v3 file is an excerpt. Definitions and counterparty limits are not visible (E1)

criteriaAssessments.assessment: A reliable June 2027 point forecast cannot be produced. At 1-12 month horizons a random walk forecasts major dollar rates as well as structural and time-series models (E13). Professional forecasters as a group do not beat it (E14). Short-horizon forecasts disagree widely, for example about 1.068 vs about 1.131 for end-November 2026 (E15). The forward premium on the old quote (about 1.37% over 263 days, about 1.91% annualised: K4, K5) has the sign covered interest parity predicts, because USD rates are above EUR rates (E9, E10, E11). Its size is only partly explained by the policy-rate gap. Parity at policy rates gives about 1.1765 against the quoted 1.1810 (K8), so most but not all of the premium is accounted for. The rest may be bank margin or term-rate expectations (E11). Either way the premium is not an expectation of euro appreciation (E12). The forecast question is therefore framed as the forward (illustratively about 1.1291 from current spot, K19) plus a range of outcomes (about 1.051 to 1.189 at 1 sigma under an assumed 8% volatility, K17, K18; see C4). In any case, s.4.2 makes a rate view irrelevant to the hedge ratio (E2).
criteriaAssessments.mechanisms: Covered interest parity is a no-arbitrage identity. The forward equals spot adjusted by the interest differential, so a higher-yielding USD means EUR/USD forwards trade above spot. Empirically the forward is a biased predictor of future spot (the Fama puzzle), and exchange-rate surprises at this horizon are dominated by news that cannot be forecast.
strengths: The forecast-accuracy literature is CORROBORATED (E13, E14)
The CIP mechanism is CORROBORATED (E12), and the sign checks out against current policy rates (E9, E10, E11)
weaknesses: The literature evidence is from search snippets. The original studies used older data and other currency pairs (E13, E14)
One cited paper suggests the sign of the Fama coefficient changed after the GFC (E12)
The size of the quoted premium is not fully reconciled with policy rates. Matched-tenor rates are needed (E11, K8)
The outcome range rests on an assumed volatility, not a market quote (E17)

criteriaAssessments.assessment: The Northbridge quote (spot 1.1650, forward 1.1810, value 2027-06-15, dated 2026-09-25) is marked 'indicative only; valid on the date of issue' (E6). Spot was about 1.12 in early November 2026 (E8), about 3.86% below the quoted spot (K7). The latest reported close in E8 is 1.1142 on 6 Nov, slightly below 1.12, so the rounded 1.12 slightly flatters current levels. The stale quote implies USD 7.086M on EUR 6M (K3). That figure is unusable. A rough parity check on the old quote, using mid policy rates, gives a fair forward of about 1.1765 against the quoted 1.1810 (K8). This suggests the bank's points may include a margin or reflect term-rate expectations (E11). It is not conclusive because policy rates are not matched-tenor OIS rates (E9, E10). An illustrative parity forward from 1.12 spot over 216 days is about 1.1291 (K19), giving about USD 6.77M (K9). That is about USD 0.31M less than the stale figure (K11). Starting from the 1.1142 print would make both the illustrative proceeds lower and the gap to the stale figure larger.
criteriaAssessments.mechanisms: Forward outright = spot + forward points. Spot moves pass almost one-for-one into the outright, so a spot fall of about 4.5 big figures makes the old outright meaningless. The points themselves depend on the term interest differential and the dealer's credit and margin charges.
strengths: The value date in the quote matches the receivable due date (E6)
The spot staleness is CORROBORATED by several reported closes (E8)
weaknesses: No live dealable forward, no bid/ask and no separate forward points are available (E6, E8)
The parity checks use policy rates, not 7-month OIS or deposit rates (E9, E10, E11)
The current spot comes from search summaries, and no 11 Nov 2026 rate was found. The latest print (1.1142) is below the rounded 1.12 used in the illustrations (E8)

criteriaAssessments.assessment: No numeric 7-month or 1-year implied volatility was found (E17). The only information is qualitative: 3-month implied vol has recently declined (E16). To give the treasurer a sense of typical outcome sizes, this section uses a clearly labelled assumed volatility of 8% annualised. That is an assumption, not market data. Over 216 days it gives a 1-sigma move of about 6.15% (K16), so June 2027 spot ranges from about 1.051 to 1.189 around 1.12 (K17, K18). Under a roughly normal approximation, about two-thirds of outcomes would fall in that band. Hedged proceeds are 6M x F plus 2M x spot at maturity, with F the illustrative parity forward of about 1.1291 (K19). Across the band they are about USD 8.88M at 1.051, USD 9.01M at 1.12 and USD 9.15M at 1.189 (K20, K21, K22). Unhedged proceeds (8M x spot at maturity) are about USD 8.41M, USD 8.96M and USD 9.51M (K23, K6, K24). The 1-sigma band is therefore about USD 0.28M wide hedged and about USD 1.10M wide unhedged (K25, K26). In sensitivity terms, each 0.01 move in EUR/USD changes proceeds by USD 20,000 hedged and USD 80,000 unhedged (K12, K13). A wider ±0.10 stress range (about 1.45 sigma under the assumed vol) gives spreads of USD 0.4M and USD 1.6M (K14, K15). All levels must be recomputed from a live forward and a market implied-vol quote.
criteriaAssessments.mechanisms: Locking in 75% at the forward rate removes three-quarters of the exchange-rate exposure, so the spread of USD outcomes shrinks in proportion. The cost is giving up the gain on the hedged portion if the euro rises. Under a random-walk view the centre of the distribution is current spot. Volatility times the square root of time sets the width.
strengths: The scenario levels and sensitivities are exact arithmetic on stated inputs and do not depend on a forecast (K12-K26)
Showing proceeds at specific rates makes the hedged-vs-unhedged tradeoff concrete
weaknesses: The 8% volatility is an assumption, not a market quote, so the band's probability content is illustrative only (E16, E17)
The forward used (about 1.1291) is a policy-rate parity proxy, not a dealable price (E9, E10, E11)
Centring on 1.12 ignores the lower 1.1142 print (E8)

criteriaAssessments.assessment: The structure is a EUR 6M forward selling EUR for USD, for value 15 June 2027, matching the receivable's due date (E1, E6). The customer's payment history, contract terms, bank credit lines and hedge-accounting election are all unknown (E21). Those facts decide whether a fixed-date forward, a window forward or a later extension or FX swap is the right tool for late payment. E18 separates two cases: a recognised receivable, and a forecasted sale that has not yet been recognised. Once the receivable is recognised, its remeasurement and the forward's mark-to-market both generally go through earnings and largely offset each other. That makes hedge accounting often optional for a receivable hedge. This offset point is general accounting background, not packet evidence. If hedge accounting is wanted, for example to cover a pre-recognition forecasted sale or to manage how forward points are presented, ASC 815 designation and documentation must be in place when the forward is executed. Forward points may be excluded from the effectiveness assessment (E18).
criteriaAssessments.mechanisms: Matching the amount and value date means the forward's EUR delivery is funded by the receivable's cash. A payment timing mismatch creates a funding gap that an FX swap or forward extension can roll. For a recognised receivable, remeasurement of the receivable and the forward's fair-value change broadly offset in earnings. Hedge-accounting documentation matters most for the forecasted-transaction phase and for how forward points are presented.
strengths: The value date in the quote already matches the due date (E6)
Hedging 75% rather than 100% leaves EUR 2M of headroom against partial non-payment (K1)
weaknesses: Timing and amount certainty, credit lines and accounting election are unknown (E21)
ASC 815 guidance was seen only in search snippets (E18). Whether the receivable is already recognised is not stated in the packet

criteriaAssessments.assessment: The governing clauses are cited (v3 s.4.1, s.4.2, s.4.3: E1, E2, E3). The arithmetic is shown in K1-K26. Assumptions are labelled, including the 8% volatility used for the scenario bands. The things that cannot be known are stated: the June 2027 spot, current implied volatility, the live forward, governance confirmation, and receivable and credit details (E17, E20, E21).
criteriaAssessments.mechanisms: Separating policy-mandated facts from market inputs, labelled assumptions and unknowns lets a reviewer check each layer independently.
strengths: Every number is reproducible from stated inputs
weaknesses: The illustrative pricing and scenario figures depend on policy-rate proxies and an assumed volatility. They must be replaced with live data (E9, E10, E17)

claims.text: Treasury Policy v3 (board-approved 2025-04-22) supersedes v1 and v2. It requires hedging 75% of confirmed foreign-currency receivables above USD 1M equivalent with maturity of 12 months or less, using forward contracts.
The required hedge amount is EUR 6M (75% of EUR 8M). The user's 50% premise would give EUR 4M, and that figure comes from the superseded v1 policy.

The E1 vs E4 contradiction is resolved in favour of v3. It is more recent (2025 vs 2021), it states that it supersedes v1, and it is board-approved. The user's 50% statement (E5) matches v1. Because it comes from an insider, it may point to a governance gap: v3 never adopted, later rescinded, or the rules changed by the unsupplied v2. The resolution therefore depends on the supplied files being genuine and current, which has not been confirmed against governance records. If confirmation cannot be obtained before the trade, executing the EUR 4M that both v1 and v3 require now, and the remaining EUR 2M once v3 is confirmed, limits the risk of trading under the wrong version.
The receivable appears to fall within s.4.1. It is described as confirmed. Its value at about 1.12 is about USD 8.96M, above USD 1M. It matures about 216 days after 11 Nov 2026, within 12 months.

The treasurer's plan to stay unhedged if she expects the euro to strengthen breaches v3 s.4.2, which bars varying hedge ratios based on management's exchange-rate views. Any deviation requires Audit Committee approval under s.4.3.
No evidence was found of a later policy version, an approved exception or an Audit Committee deviation for this exposure. Whether one exists cannot be determined from the packet.
A reliable point forecast of EUR/USD for June 2027 cannot be determined. At 1-12 month horizons, models and professional forecasters generally do not beat a random walk on point accuracy.

The forward premium in the old quote (about 1.37% over 263 days, about 1.91% annualised) has the sign covered interest parity predicts, because USD rates exceed EUR rates. Its size is only partly explained by the policy-rate gap: parity at policy rates gives about 1.1765 against the quoted 1.1810, and the rest may be margin or term-rate expectations. The premium is not a market expectation that the euro will rise.

The 2026-09-25 Northbridge quote is stale and indicative. Spot has fallen from 1.1650 to about 1.12 (about -3.86%), and the latest reported close was lower still at 1.1142 on 6 Nov 2026. So the USD 7.086M implied by EUR 6M x 1.1810 cannot be relied on. The E6 vs E8 contradiction is resolved in favour of E8 for current market levels because E8 is about seven weeks more recent and is corroborated by several reports. E6 remains valid as a record of the September price.

A rough parity check using mid policy rates gives a fair forward of about 1.1765 on the old 1.1650 spot, against the quoted 1.1810. The bank's points may include a margin or reflect term-rate expectations, but policy rates are not matched-tenor rates and the rates in force on 2026-09-25 may have differed.

As an illustration only, a parity forward from about 1.12 spot over 216 days at mid policy rates is about 1.1291. That would lock in about USD 6.77M on EUR 6M, about USD 0.31M less than the stale-quote figure. Starting from the later 1.1142 close would make the illustrative proceeds lower and the gap larger. The actual amount must come from a live dealable quote.
Current numeric EUR/USD implied volatility for a 7-month or 1-year tenor is not available, so market-based probability bands cannot be produced. Any band shown rests on an assumed volatility.

With 75% hedged, each 0.01 move in EUR/USD changes total USD proceeds by USD 20,000, against USD 80,000 fully unhedged. Over a hypothetical ±0.10 stress range (about 1.45 sigma under an assumed 8% volatility) the outcome spread is USD 0.4M hedged vs USD 1.6M unhedged.

For a recognised EUR receivable, the receivable's remeasurement and the forward's mark-to-market generally both go through earnings and largely offset. This is general accounting background, not packet evidence. Hedge accounting is therefore often optional, and its absence is not a major earnings risk. If hedge accounting is wanted, for example for a pre-recognition forecasted sale, which E18 treats separately, ASC 815 designation and documentation must be in place when the forward is executed. Forward points may be excluded from the effectiveness assessment.
The customer's payment reliability, the certainty of the 15 June 2027 timing, bank credit lines for forwards and the company's hedge-accounting election cannot be determined from the packet.

Under an assumed (not market-quoted) 8% annualised volatility, a 1-sigma range for June 2027 EUR/USD around 1.12 is about 1.051 to 1.189. Across that range, total USD proceeds are about USD 8.88M / 9.01M / 9.15M with the 75% hedge at the illustrative 1.1291 forward, against about USD 8.41M / 8.96M / 9.51M unhedged. The 1-sigma band is about USD 0.28M wide hedged and about USD 1.10M wide unhedged.

alternatives.comparison: Hedges EUR 2M less than v3 requires and leaves EUR 4M exposed (USD 40,000 per 0.01 move instead of USD 20,000). Non-compliant with v3 s.4.1 unless the Audit Committee approves it under s.4.3 (E1, E3, E4).

alternatives.option: Stay unhedged on a euro-strengthening view
alternatives.comparison: Full exposure of USD 80,000 per 0.01 move (K13), and a 1-sigma proceeds band about USD 1.10M wide under the assumed volatility (K26). Explicitly barred by s.4.2 (E2). The view itself has no demonstrated forecasting basis (E13, E14).
Removes all exchange-rate variance but exceeds the 75% ratio. It is also a deviation under s.4.3, and it carries over-hedge risk if the customer pays late or only partly (E3, E21).

alternatives.option: Use FX options (buy EUR puts) instead of forwards
alternatives.comparison: Keeps the upside if the euro rises, but costs a premium that cannot be quantified without implied volatility (E17). s.4.1 specifies forwards, so options need Audit Committee approval (E1, E3).

alternatives.option: Window forward or fixed forward plus later FX swap or extension
alternatives.comparison: A window forward allows flexibility on settlement timing at some extra cost. A fixed 15 June forward that is rolled by swap if payment slips is cheaper upfront. Which is better depends on payment-history data that is not available (E21).

tradeoffs: The 75% forward gives certainty on EUR 6M of proceeds but gives up any gain on that portion if EUR/USD rises above the locked rate (E1, K12).
The 25% unhedged residual keeps some upside and gives a cushion against partial non-payment, but leaves about USD 20,000 of exposure per 0.01 move (K12).
Executing quickly reduces further drift from the stale quote. Waiting for full credit-line and accounting confirmation reduces execution risk (E6, E8, E21).
edgeCasesAndFailureModes: The customer pays late. The forward settles on 15 June 2027 without EUR cash to deliver, so an FX swap or extension is needed, and its points reflect the interest differential at that time (E21).
The customer pays partly or defaults. A EUR 6M forward could exceed the cash received if more than EUR 2M is not paid, leaving an over-hedge exposed to exchange-rate moves (E21, K1).

The forward is executed before the sale is recognised as a receivable, and no ASC 815 documentation is in place. The forward's mark-to-market then hits earnings with no offsetting remeasurement until the receivable is booked. Once the receivable is recognised, the two broadly offset in earnings, so the accounting risk is mainly in that pre-recognition period (E18).
No available credit line with the counterparty. The forward cannot be executed as planned (E21).
A later policy version, a rescission or an approved exception exists that is not in the packet. The 75% conclusion would then change (E20).
The supplied policy files are not genuine or are misordered. The supersession reasoning fails (E20).
The bank prices with a wide margin. Checking parity against live OIS rates is needed to detect this (E11).

counterarguments.argument: The treasurer has good reason to think the euro will strengthen, so hedging locks in a worse rate.
counterarguments.response: s.4.2 bars varying the ratio on management views (E2). Professional forecasters generally do not beat a random walk (E14). If she has a strong case, the route is an Audit Committee deviation request under s.4.3 (E3), not a unilateral choice.

counterarguments.argument: The forward at 1.1810 is above spot, so the market expects the euro to rise and staying unhedged captures that.
counterarguments.response: The sign of the premium is what covered interest parity predicts from the USD-EUR interest differential, and any excess over parity looks like margin or term-rate effects, not a forecast (E11, E12, K8). Forwards are poor predictors of future spot (E12). The quote is also stale, since spot has fallen to about 1.12 (E8).

counterarguments.argument: The user is an insider and says the policy is 50%. That may mean v3 was never adopted, was rescinded, or that v2 (not supplied) changed the rules, so v1's 50% may really be in force.
counterarguments.response: This is a real possibility that the packet cannot rule out (E20). v2 is missing and v3 has not been checked against board minutes. On the documents supplied, though, v3 is board-approved, later, and explicitly supersedes v1 and v2 (E1, E4). The right step is to confirm v3's status with the policy owner or board minutes before trading. If that cannot be done in time, executing the EUR 4M that both v1 and v3 require (K2) now, and the remaining EUR 2M (K12 basis: EUR 8M - EUR 6M = EUR 2M unhedged under v3, and EUR 6M - EUR 4M = EUR 2M extra) once v3 is confirmed, limits the risk of trading under the wrong version. If v3 is confirmed, that interval is a temporary under-hedge, so confirmation should be fast.

counterarguments.argument: Without implied volatility the hedge decision cannot be quantified, so it should wait.
counterarguments.response: The policy sets the ratio regardless of volatility (E1, E2). Volatility affects only the scenario illustration and option pricing (E17), not the forward-hedge requirement.

correctedUserAssumptions.correction: The 50% figure is from v1 (2021). v3 (board-approved 2025-04-22) supersedes it and requires 75% for this receivable, which is EUR 6M, using forwards. This is subject to confirming that v3 is in force and was not rescinded (E20).

practicalImplications: Get a live, dealable EUR/USD forward quote for value 2027-06-15 for EUR 6M, ideally from more than one bank, and check the points against matched-tenor EUR and USD OIS rates (E6, E11).
Do not use the USD 7.086M figure from the 2026-09-25 quote in budgets or forecasts (E6, E8, K3).
Confirm with the policy owner or board minutes that v3 is in force, was not rescinded, and that no exception exists before execution (E20).
If the treasurer wants to hedge less than 75% or use options, submit a written deviation request to the Audit Committee under s.4.3 instead of acting unilaterally (E2, E3).
Complete ASC 815 hedge designation and documentation at or before trade execution if hedge accounting is desired, especially if the sale is not yet recognised as a receivable (E18).
Confirm credit-line availability with the counterparty and agree in advance how a late payment will be handled (swap or extension) (E21).

The content of v2, which was not supplied (E4).
The live spot and forward for value 2027-06-15. The current spot (~1.12, last reported close 1.1142) comes only from search summaries (E8).
Matched-tenor EUR and USD interest rates, and the rates in force on 2026-09-25. The parity checks use October policy rates as proxies (E9, E10, E11).
Current 7-month or 1-year EUR/USD implied volatility. The scenario bands use an assumed 8% that may differ materially from market (E17).
Receivable payment reliability and timing, whether the receivable is already recognised, credit lines and hedge-accounting election (E21, E18).
Whether s.4.1 maturity is measured from booking or from hedge date. Both appear to be within 12 months (E19).
furtherResearchThatCouldChangeConclusion: Board minutes or governance records showing that v3 is not in force, or a later policy, rescission or approved Audit Committee exception, could change the required hedge ratio (E20).

Contract terms or customer payment history showing significant risk of late or partial payment could justify a smaller or window-structured forward, through an Audit Committee deviation if it falls below 75% (E21, E3).
Evidence that the receivable matures more than 12 months out, or is not confirmed, would take it outside s.4.1 (E19).
Live OIS-based pricing showing the bank's forward points are materially off-market would change the counterparty choice but not the ratio (E11).
A numeric implied-volatility quote would replace the assumed 8% in the outcome bands and allow option-cost comparisons (E17).
